items.description: The Argo CD sync-failed alert no longer expires after 5 minutes while the app stays failed. An auto-synced app whose sync failed, and that Argo CD no longer retries, raises a standing alert. The alert stays up until the app next syncs successfully, then resolves (Ruling D1). An app synced by hand keeps the immediate event only (Ruling D1's limit).
evidence: ArgoCDDeploy/config/prd/values.yaml:92-102: app-sync-failed carries labels, annotations and generatorURL only
argoproj/notifications-engine pkg/services/alertmanager.go:29-34,77: AlertmanagerNotification has StartsAt (set to time.Now()) and no EndsAt
argoproj/argo-cd v3.5.1 controller/appcontroller.go:2396-2399: SyncError condition when auto-sync declines to retry a failed revision
argoproj/argo-cd v3.5.1 controller/appcontroller.go:2332-2334: auto-sync returns before the SyncError check for an app without automated sync

items.description: `on-health-degraded` has the same shape and is fixed the same way. An app that Argo CD reports Degraded for longer than a transient dip raises a standing alert. The alert stays up until the app's health leaves Degraded, then resolves.
evidence: ArgoCDDeploy/config/prd/values.yaml:103-112,122-126: app-health-degraded template and on-health-degraded trigger, same event shape as the sync-failed one

items.area: R1 — D7's events without a false resolve
items.description: D7's immediate events still arrive as today: ArgoCDSyncFailed is critical and carries Argo CD's error text, and ArgoCDHealthDegraded is a warning. Their expiry no longer sends a "resolved". Every other alert still sends its resolved message (Ruling D1).

PrometheusDeploy/config/prd/values.yaml:351-367: telegram-critical and telegram-warning both send_resolved: true

items.area: R1 — standing alert edges and routing, proven by the test verb
items.description: PrometheusDeploy's test verb (`kc project test`, no Jenkins stage) proves the standing alerts offline with promtool unit tests over synthetic series, with a firing and a quiet case for each edge (Ruling T1). The standing alerts arrive only after Argo CD's own retries, never while it is syncing or retrying. They do not fire on D5 drift, and the failed-sync alert does not fire on an app waiting for a manual sync. Their identity is the app, not the scrape target. A metrics gap neither resolves nor re-fires them. The same verb asserts, against the rendered Alertmanager config and without amtool, which receiver each alert reaches, that D7's two events send no resolve, and that every other alert still does.
evidence: ArgoCDDeploy/chart/templates/applicationsets.yaml:53-57: auto-synced entries retry 3 times, 30s doubling
live 2026-09-25 (kubectl get applications -n argocd-prd): 49 of 50 Applications auto-sync; argocd-prd does not
PrometheusDeploy/.kubecoder/project.yaml:15-23: the test verb today renders the charts, plans the Terraform and runs the architecture checks; nothing reads the rules

items.description: argo-cd D7 stands and carries Ruling D1 as an amendment. The notification is the event, and its expiry sends no resolve. The Prometheus rule is the standing state. The standing failed-sync alert covers auto-synced apps only, and the standing degraded alert covers every app.
evidence: AnsibleSpecs/argo-cd/decisions.md:59-63: D7 as it stands

items.area: R3 — ANS-26 transient provider checksum fetches

items.area: R5 — ANS-105 gitblit prunes stale gb_lucene.conf entries
items.description: gitblit prunes stale branch entries from gb_lucene.conf so indexing does not stall. At pod start, the `clean-lucene-locks` init container drops each `[aliases]`/`[branches]` entry whose branch is not in that repository's `gitblit.indexBranch`. It never drops an entry Gitblit still indexes, and the lock cleanup is unchanged.
evidence: GitSyncDeploy/chart/templates/gitblit-deployment.yaml:29-40: clean-lucene-locks (busybox) deletes only write.lock and gb_lucene.conf.lock*
DockerImages/git-sync/git-sync.sh:42-75: gitblit.indexBranch kept as full ref names via git config --add/--unset
gitblit-org/gitblit LuceneService.updateIndex (deletedBranches loop) and LuceneRepoIndexStore (lucene/<version>/gb_lucene.conf): aliases never removed

items.area: R5 — prune proven offline, no git
items.description: GitSyncDeploy's test verb (`kc project test`, no Jenkins stage) proves the prune offline (Ruling T1). A script under `tests/` runs, under busybox in the iac toolchain, the prune the init container runs. Its fixture is laid out like the volume. Stale entries go, live entries stay, a default branch spelled `default` included, and a second run changes nothing. The prune uses nothing the busybox image lacks, so no git.
evidence: GitSyncDeploy/.kubecoder/project.yaml:16-23: the test verb today renders the chart, plans the Terraform and runs the architecture checks
GitSyncDeploy/chart/templates/gitblit-deployment.yaml:31: the init container image is unpinned busybox
